title: Exploratory DAL task frame versus nominal role marking in the complete f45r.8-11 paragraph
summary: Two actually authored partial constructions share one unassigned DAL core. F1 links the written otydal daiin introduction to explicit daldaiin through one task, goal and procedure; N1 reuses free/bound nominal role markers in otydal daiin, dor or and kol dy. All32 IT groups remain. No selected reading or word value; reference, parsing and scope assumptions stay explicit.
selection_note: The family, full page and local daldaiin background were examined on8October. This work authors explicit competing bindings on that retained paragraph; it does not rediscover forms or rerun counts. No general suffix decoder or fixed statistical test is selected.

source_lines.raw_text: tchol cthy qodaiin cthy dain cthey otydal daiin m
dor or chain dain ykolody ytaiin qotchol kol dy
okaiin shar yky oky kair daldy dalor cheol dal

F1.core: D is one unassigned reusable task/process schema with associated procedure A_D and target condition Z_D. No material, physical property, plant, quantity or action word has been chosen.
F1.common_content_relation: A_D is the procedure prescribed for attaining Z_D on its bound argument. Successful execution entails Z_D afterward under the same task definition. This is stipulated schema content; if success merely means attainment it is definitional, not evidence. A request does not assert execution or success.
lexical_and_binding_rules: Exact otydal followed by the next complete raw group A introduces frame(D,x,descriptor=A). In this paragraph A is the whole daiin at .8G008. x is an unassigned referent of that descriptor, not a person or substance named by us.
daldy names the target condition Z_D for the active frame; it does not assert the current or achieved state.
dalor names the associated procedure A_D in that same frame; no independent material or result noun is assigned.
Bare dal requests A_D on the active x.

Exact daldaiin is hypothetically parsed as dal+daiin and expresses a request for D with an explicit argument descriptor. Within this frame, matching the stored daiin descriptor reuses x by a declared local reference rule, not by universal same-spelling identity.
F1.scope: Frame starts after the complete otydal-A pair and persists to the own-marked paragraph end. Unknown groups do not silently create a new frame in this partial construction. Their actual effects are unresolved; preserving the frame across them is an assumption. No first-word paragraph topic is inherited from C1.
F1.occurrence_identity: The bare and incorporated requests are two written request occurrences with corresponding D/x content. They are not merged into one inscription, counted as two executions, or translated as again. Whether they refer to one intended performance is not established.
F1.participant_identity: The first descriptor and its later embedded spelling are distinct written occurrences. Their local x-binding is an assumption of F1; no global daiin individual, proper name or unique material is inferred.
whole_paragraph_rendering: [tchol cthy qodaiin cthy dain cthey] {otydal daiin: introduce task D on x} [m]
[dor or chain dain ykolody ytaiin qotchol kol dy]
[okaiin shar yky oky kair] {daldy: D target condition} {dalor: D procedure} [cheol] {dal: request D on x}
[l okaiin okcho laldan] {daldaiin: request D with explicit descriptor daiin, locally resolved to x}
known_limits: All five family functions, the procedure/goal association, right-one-group introduction and later reference rule are new working assumptions, not recovered meanings.
No role is supplied for26groups. cheol, m and the repeated cthy/dain/okaiin cannot be treated as semantically empty; their later interpretation may change or contradict the frame.

The rule is worked through only for the explicitly delimited frame. The single exact otydal cannot be used to claim coverage of all16 IT daldy occurrences on15selectors. Labels and other occurrences remain obligations, not new hidden introductions.
The known singleton daldy label at f75v.32 blocks a universal requirement for an additional written label argument. F1 does not supply an interpretation for every such label.
The other daldaiin locus was already inspected; this draft does not claim to explain it or the ordinary/fused daiin forms elsewhere.
This is not a universal uniquely decodable writer for arbitrary D/A strings. Extension to other argument descriptors would need to address collisions with the declared family forms.

N1.core: D is an unassigned nominal kind/description N_D, not an automatically fixed individual. This is a different lexical-type hypothesis from F1 and is not mixed into it.
N1.type_contract: ROLE_s takes a nominal description N and returns ArgSpec(description=N,role=R_s), for s in {or,dy,daiin}. The three R_s are unassigned grammatical role tags, not translations such as from, with, number or amount. A governing predicate and its role meanings remain unread.
N1.one_binding_rule: A free licensed marker s applies to the immediately preceding complete nominal head; the licensed fused DAL+s form contributes the same ArgSpec as that head plus the marker. The shared contribution is hypothetical, not proved by spacing.
licensed_internal_analyses: otydal = N_OTY(D), a proposed nominal modification preserving the D description; the contribution of oty is not assigned

three_explicit_host_pairs.fused_comparison: daldaiin = ROLE_daiin(N_D); the oty qualification differs and is not deleted

N1.productivity_boundary: This partial version licenses only the named internal DAL analyses and the three explicit free-marker applications. dor, kol and otydal are proposed nominal hosts, not confirmed nouns. It is not a rule that every ending match is an identical suffix.
unresolved_productive_extension: A productive suffix parser must also consider dor=d+or, qodaiin=qo+daiin and ykolody=ykolo+dy. It must not exclude them merely to improve a result.

If dor is already ArgSpec(d,R_or), the following free or asks for a nominal input under the stated single-role type. No stacking, overwriting, idempotence or silent reset is supplied. This alternative parse is unresolved.
ykolody is not literally kol+dy; its extra material is not removed. qodaiin is not pooled with standalone daiin.

GDT1047 already contradicts an unchanged universal paragraph-local left-host requirement for exact daiin in IT at f28v.6 andf58v.30; ZL flags differ. This local construction cannot be exported as that exceptionless rule.
N1.identity: No same-individual link is inferred among the five D-bearing expressions. Marking a role neither creates a new object nor supplies a predicate or result state.
whole_paragraph_rendering: [tchol cthy qodaiin cthy dain cthey] {otydal daiin: ROLE_daiin(N_OTY(D))} [m]
{dor or: ROLE_or(N_dor)} [chain dain ykolody ytaiin qotchol] {kol dy: ROLE_dy(N_kol)}
[okaiin shar yky oky kair] {daldy: ROLE_dy(N_D)} {dalor: ROLE_or(N_D)} [cheol] {dal: N_D}

concrete_disagreement: At otydal daiin, F1 treats the whole daiin as an explicit argument descriptor of a task. N1 treats it as a marker on the preceding nominal expression. At final daldaiin, F1 preserves that descriptor inside a request; N1 assigns a grammatical role to N_D. These are different compositional and referential commitments, not two German synonyms.
comparison_ceiling: F1 explains a hypothetical reference thread; N1 explains a hypothetical distribution of marking between free and fused forms. Neither reads the complete paragraph. Their unequal conditional coverage and complexity do not rank historical plausibility or establish a meaning.
reader_sensitivity: IT and ZL have exact otydal daiin with definite boundaries at .8G007-008. RF has @221;tydal daiin; the entity is not converted to o.
The .10 line and final .11 l okaiin okcho laldan daldaiin are exact across all three readings. These are alternatives of one manuscript.
IT/ZL own flags mark .8 as start and.11 as end. RF has no corresponding flags, so its frame scope is unresolved.
N1 dor or is exact in IT; ZL has @201;or or and RF dor @221;r. The free-marker pair is not made reader-unanimous.
kol dy is exact in all three. .8G006 andG009 differ among readers; all unknown/annotated groups remain. No drawing interruptions or uncertain inner gaps are stored in these four lines.

profile_account.scope: Existing exact whole-group profiles over179 admitted selectors, readers separate; embedded strings are not standalone counts.
constraints: dal is broad across all sections, so no local narrow content is chosen.
daldy is prose and label material, never physically line-initial in these profiles; these positions do not identify its part of speech.
dalor is medial prose in the retained scope, not thereby a two-argument relation.
daiin is very frequent, broadly distributed and repeats adjacent to itself; no numeral, conjunction or argument category is established by frequency.
The same-string/local-reference choices above are hypothetical. All old measured-material, thermal, quantity, stirring and conjunction glosses remain frozen, not inherited facts.
or and dy both recur as adjacent exact repeats and at different physical line positions. No generic stacking rule follows; N1 has not covered their full distributions.
dor and kol have broad retained prose contexts. Their proposed local nominal-head types are hypotheses, not known meanings or parts of speech.

prior_limits: 1198/1208 establish retained form/context and one informed physical-body observation, not a semantic stem.1198 has no identical full two-sided frame for dal/daly/daldy.
1200 provides repeated-base families and the ololdy ambiguity.1201 transparent chunking preserves stipulated content; it does not prove joined/split meaning identity here.
788 chiefly tests Xdal remainder transfer, with limited success; it neither proves nor generally refutes this specific dalY family. The old655 measured-material default is not reused.
WE019/877/907 retain literal dal daiin and daldaiin comparisons without selecting semantic equivalence or a universal seam rule.

951/953 already developed abstract statement/action/property coupling. The present limited native frame is an application, not a claim to invent that general mechanism; their physical-writing failures remain.
C1 positive-scope consistency selection stays parked. Neither new construction is validated merely because it lacks an internal contradiction.
decision: Retain both explicit partial constructions for development, with no winner or new translated word. Do not infer a global lexicon from this one framed paragraph. Future extension must preserve the declared D content, distinguish argument from marker, account for the other retained contexts and explain actual remaining words rather than add unmarked repairs.
work_done: Eight bounded agents retrieved only relevant prior evidence, authored two actual alternatives and independently checked source/binding/type limits. Root applied both to all32rawgroups with every residual preserved. No new data admission, statistical model, large parser or reserved confirmation.
access: Existing admitted exposed source caches and primaries only. f84/f84r remain sealed; reserves and f116v not opened.
